questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Culture and completely different people and way of thinking. Relatively high academic standards and international recognition.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. As with most things you are completely confused when first showing up but it only takes a short time to get used to it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Most communication through e-mail and the university is really quick in answering if any questions. Other exchange students were also a big help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many many different options as NUS is massive. uTown is the best but other campus housings were also fine. Difference also if you had meal plans or not.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I didn't chose meal plan which I am really happy with. The food looked bad although it sounds easy. There are plenty of food courts all over campus where you can choose more freely your meals. Food is generally quite bad. Cooking facilities were almost none excisting.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's very small and disqusting in some places. Definitily don't be delicate. But it is super cheap and all other exchange students live there so definitly chose this option.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is divided into multiple rounds depending on the amount of credit needed. In the first round I only got half my courses so I had to apply for the second round as well. It was hard to get the exact courses that I wanted but in the end I was only worried about getting enough credits.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mail and guides were enough.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be picky in what courses you want and follow the deadlines.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very different approach to learning (more boring in my opinion). Local students were extreme students studying all the time making it a bit stressful because we are graded on the belcurve.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: We could only choose BA classes. The level itself was low but because the local students were studying all the time the level rose.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much less group work and cases and more the teacher just explaining for the whole class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Space Law
Carriage of Goods by Sea
Aviation Law and Policy
Multinational Enterprises and International Law

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Aviation Law and Policy is the best course I have ever had! The professor is amazing and the course is full of exchange students. Readings are many but fairly easy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and housing on campus was cheaper than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost any sport or social activity. You just had to find it yourself.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Choose your sport and write to them yourself. Most clubs are just for the locals so when asking it is a great way to get local friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Sport, exploring the city and TRAVEL!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Everybody speaks english so that was easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs and practice your sport. They don't want to socialize over studying.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Food and interests besides the study.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Clear rules for everything.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be aware of the deadlines for housing to make sure you get a spot on campus.
2. Eat at the food courts for cheap food.
3. Don't take school too serious, it will be fine with minimal amount of study. Use the time to travel the region.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you arrive 1 week prior to the beginning of the courses you will have time to socialize and meet other students. Not necessary from an academic point of view.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living and proving to myself that I can live by myself in such a foreign country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: No major challenges really.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
